mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations diminish.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases by > 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within a month signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending power and confidence increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where UNRATE decreases by > 0.3% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, inflationary pressures and tightening monetary policy lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) also decline in the same month, a dual demand shock leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% and RSAFS declines in the same month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST declines > 10% and RSAFS declines in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% and a simultaneous decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within a month signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where INDPRO increases > 1% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% within a month.
